Ticket Info:
Sponsor: Marin Center
Link: http://www.marincounty.org/depts/cu
The Frank Lloyd Wright-designed Marin County Civic Center is a national- and state-designated historic landmark. Ninety minute docent-led tours of the Civic Center are offered every Wednesday and Friday at 10:30 am, leaving from the second floor Café, Room 233. The cost is $10 adults and $5 seniors and students. No reservations are required. Groups of ten or more can arrange a private docent tour by calling the Visitor Services Office at \(415\) 473-3762.

item.title: Ultimate Heirloom Apple Tasting Experience at Gold Ridge Organic Farms — Fri Sep 18, 2:00 PM — Gold Ridge Organic Farms
item.description:
Start with a guided walk through our organic apple orchards, where guests will learn how our trees are grown and what apples and people have in common \(hint: no two are alike\). Enjoy the expansive views of the rolling hills and farms surrounding our 88-acre property in southwest Sebastopol.
Then, enjoy a side-by-side tasting of four to five hand-picked heirloom apples, paired with local artisan cheeses drizzled with our apple cider syrup and a taste of freshly pressed apple juice.
This is a limited-time experience offered only during harvest season, when our apples are at their peak. Spaces are limited, so we encourage you to book soon and secure your spot for an unforgettable afternoon celebrating the magic of heirloom apples.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: A Conversation with Reverend Deborah Lee — Fri Sep 18, 6:00 PM — Petaluma Museum
item.description:
An evening of film, conversation, and community dialogue exploring displacement, immigrant justice, and what genuine security can look like.
How do we create communities where everyone feels safe, welcome, and able to belong?
Join Rev. Deborah Lee, Co-Executive Director of the Interfaith Movement for Human Integrity, and Petaluma filmmaker Lina Hoshino for an evening of film, conversation, and community dialogue exploring displacement, immigrant justice, and what genuine security can look like.
The evening begins with a screening of selected excerpts from the award-winning 2011 documentary Living Along the Fenceline, a film created in collaboration with Rev. Lee and Hoshino that examines the human impact of militarized borders and the communities living alongside them. Following the screening, the filmmakers will reflect on the film's enduring relevance and invite audience members into a thoughtful conversation and Q&A.

item.title: Estate Dinners at Darioush — Fri Sep 18, 6:00 PM
item.description:
Estate Dinners at Darioush invite guests to enjoy elegant al fresco evenings overlooking the estate vineyards. Each dinner features a thoughtfully crafted multi-course menu by the Estate Chef, inspired by the seasonal bounty of Napa Valley and the Khaledi family's favorite global summer flavors. Every course is expertly paired with limited-release Darioush wines, including Signature Viognier, Sauvignon Blanc, estate reds, and library vintages of Signature Cabernet Sauvignon. Guests will also hear from Vice President of Winemaking Michael Tracy, who shares insights into the vineyards, the upcoming vintage, and the artistry behind each wine. With exceptional cuisine, distinguished wines, and breathtaking vineyard views, the Estate Dinners offer an unforgettable celebration of Napa Valley hospitality.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Summer Movie Nights in the Grove at Raymond — Fri Sep 18, 6:00 PM — Raymond Vineyards

Part of the Summer Movie Nights in the Grove series, this relaxed experience combines a beloved movie musical with wine, light bites, and the beautiful setting of the vineyard. Guests can purchase wine by the glass or bottle and enjoy additional bites throughout the evening while taking in the film beneath the night sky. Bring a blanket, gather your friends, and settle into the Grove for a nostalgic evening of great wine, good company, and cinematic fun. Whether you’re a longtime fan of La La Land or simply looking for a unique way to enjoy a summer evening in Napa Valley, this outdoor movie night offers the perfect combination of entertainment and wine country ambiance.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market — Sat Sep 19, 12:00 AM — Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
item.description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Playbook delivers a first-of-its-kind sports destination for the Bay Area, featuring a larger-than-life wraparound halo screen broadcasting the action throughout the venue.
